threads.body: [General] `execInContainer` returns a nonzero `ExecResult` rather than throwing when the producer command fails. Ignoring that result treats a failed produce as success, so this setup no longer guarantees the sample operation intended to create flush metrics and later failures become opaque metric timeouts. Check the exit code and report stdout/stderr.

[General] Avoid running this broker-only producer in `CONNECT` mode. That container launches only `connect-distributed` and has no broker at `localhost:9092`, so the producer waits for metadata and then fails, adding a long and unnecessary delay to `KafkaConnectTest`. Invoke it only for the KRaft and ZooKeeper modes.
no longer necessary as the rules syntax is automatically tested by `TargetSystemTest` and we add an integration test to cover this.

for now the metric assertions test the metrics "as they currently are", improving the metrics (and adding weaver validation) will be covered by https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/issues/14279

As those definitions use the `experimental-` prefix in the target system, there should not be expectations for them to be stable, so we can improve them in a secondary step.
all of this plumbing has been moved to `KafkaContainer` to allow reusing.
without this in older 2.x kafka there are no log flush metrics produced, this is no longer the case with 3.x

zookeeper setup is being deprecated and will be removed in 4.x, so it's probably not worth testing explicit for it, we only test it with a "legacy" image provided by bitnami that uses slightly different config options.

This setup is how it is currently tested [in jmx-scraper](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-contrib/blob/main/jmx-metrics/src/integrationTest/java/io/opentelemetry/contrib/jmxmetrics/target_systems/KafkaIntegrationTest.java) and will be extended to support both producer and consumer variants when adding them.

Testcontainers checks only the ports registered on the container, and none are registered here, so `Wait.forListeningPort()` returns at once and Kafka can start before ZooKeeper is listening.

```suggestion
      GenericContainer<?> zookeeper =
          new GenericContainer<>(zookeeperImage)
              .withNetworkAliases("zookeeper")
              .withExposedPorts(2181)
              .withStartupTimeout(Duration.ofMinutes(1))
              .waitingFor(Wait.forListeningPort());
```

`withStartupTimeout` applies to the wait strategy that exists when it is called, and every `configure*()` method then calls `waitingFor(...)`, which installs a new strategy and drops it. KRaft and ZooKeeper mode therefore run on the 60-second default, and raising this value later would change nothing; set the timeout on the strategy passed to `waitingFor` instead, as `configureKafkaConnect` does. (Same ordering on the ZooKeeper container in `KafkaBrokerTest`.)

[General] `waitingFor` replaces the strategy that `withStartupTimeout` configured, so this timeout cannot affect the ZooKeeper container. Set it on the replacement strategy, as `KafkaContainer` does.

```suggestion
      GenericContainer<?> zookeeper =
          new GenericContainer<>(zookeeperImage)
              .withNetworkAliases("zookeeper")
              .withExposedPorts(2181)
              .waitingFor(Wait.forListeningPort().withStartupTimeout(Duration.ofMinutes(1)));
```

[Style] `KafkaContainer` is used only by tests in this package, so package-private is the most restrictive modifier that works, like `WeaverContainer`. (Same for `create`, `withZookeeper`, and `withKafkaConnect`.)

```suggestion
class KafkaContainer extends GenericContainer<KafkaContainer> {
```

[Testing] Kafka Connect waited up to 5 minutes for `/connectors` before this refactor, and 1 minute can time out on a loaded CI runner.

